order_source.title: Order source
order_source.subtitle: Where the service learns about the store's orders and refunds. A store has one source: a REST API key or the plugin.

api.why: The simplest way: nothing is installed in your store. The service reads orders and refunds through the WooCommerce REST API with a read-only key.
api.step_open: In the WordPress admin open WooCommerce → Settings → Advanced → REST API and click "Add key".
api.step_permissions: Description "Business Watchdog", user — a store administrator or shop manager, permissions "Read". Click "Generate API key".
api.step_paste: Copy the Consumer key and Consumer secret here — WooCommerce shows them only once.
api.requirements: Required: the store address on HTTPS and permalinks other than "Plain" (Settings → Permalinks).
api.key_hint: The key starts with ck_ followed by 40 characters.
api.secret_hint: The secret starts with cs_ followed by 40 characters.
api.access_title: What the service sees and what it cannot do
api.access_reads: Reads orders (number, status, amount, currency, payment method, payment reference, dates) and refunds.
api.access_not_read: Does not keep customers, addresses, phone numbers or products: the service does not request those fields.
api.access_scope: A "Read" key can technically read other store data too, but the service only calls orders and refunds.
api.access_no_write: Nothing in the store can be changed with such a key. The service refuses keys with write permission.
api.access_frequency: Reading: changes every 5 minutes, recent orders hourly, a full 90-day check daily; at most 60 requests at a time.
api.access_revoke: Disconnect here or delete the key in WooCommerce — the service stops reading immediately.
api.verifies_store: Connecting a working key also confirms the store — no DNS record needed.
api.late_refunds_warning: On WooCommerce older than 7.9, a refund added to an older order reaches the service up to an hour later.
api.mode_warning: Without the plugin, Stripe test and live payments cannot be told apart: with a test-mode provider such orders are not supported in this mode — the plugin is needed.
api.polling_note: The service polls the store itself: changes every 5 minutes.
api.key_rejected: The store no longer accepts the key (it was deleted or its permissions changed). Reading has stopped — create a new "Read" key, disconnect the old one and connect the new one.
api.revoke_warning: The service deletes the key on its side and stops reading orders. Delete the key in WooCommerce too (Settings → Advanced → REST API).
api.plugin_active: Orders currently come through the plugin. A store has one order source: to switch to a REST API key, first disconnect the plugin in the "Plugin" tab.

shopware.why: Nothing has to be set up by hand in the store: the service reads Shopware 6.6 and 6.7 orders through the Admin API — with the app or an integration key.
shopware.step_role: In the admin open Settings → System → Users & permissions → Roles and create a role "Business Watchdog" with a single permission: Orders → View.
shopware.step_integration: Open Settings → System → Integrations → Add integration: name "Business Watchdog", "Administrator" off, assign the new role. Save.
shopware.step_paste: Copy the Access key ID and Secret access key here — Shopware shows the secret only once.
shopware.requirements: Required: the store address on HTTPS where the Admin API (/api) is reachable.
shopware.access_reads: Reads orders: number, status, amount, currency, payment method, payment status and PayPal payment reference.
shopware.access_not_read: Does not request customers, addresses or products — the service limits the response fields explicitly.
shopware.access_calls: Sends only the token request and order searches; nothing is changed in the store.
shopware.state_risk: Important: in Shopware 6.6 and 6.7 even a key with a "view only" role can technically change order, payment and delivery statuses (a Shopware limitation, reported to the developers). It cannot move money or edit orders. The service never sends such requests and keeps the key encrypted. Keep the key secret.
shopware.acknowledge: I understand: the key can change statuses; the service only uses it for reading
shopware.state_risk_short: The key can technically change order statuses — keep it secret; the service only reads.
shopware.refunds_note: Shopware records a refund only as the payment status: for a partial refund the amount is shown from the payment provider (PayPal), and the check against the store is "no data".
shopware.key_rejected: Shopware no longer accepts the key (the integration was deleted or its role changed). Reading has stopped — create a new integration and connect it.
shopware.revoke_warning: The service deletes the key on its side and stops reading orders. Delete the integration in Shopware too (Settings → System → Integrations).
shopware.method_app_hint: Upload the app file in Shopware — Shopware shows the read-only permissions at install, no keys to copy, changes arrive right away.
shopware.method_key_hint: Create a role and an integration by hand and paste the key; changes are read every 5 minutes.
shopware.app_step_download: Download the app file for this store (button below).
shopware.app_step_upload: In the Shopware admin open Extensions → My extensions → Upload extension and choose BusinessWatchdog.zip.
shopware.app_step_install: Click Install, then Activate and confirm the permissions — the connection completes by itself.
shopware.app_permissions: The app only asks to read orders, payments, currencies and payment methods. The file is made for this store; a new file replaces a previous one that is not installed yet.
shopware.app_downloaded: App file downloaded. Upload it in Shopware.
shopware.app_waiting: Waiting for the app to be installed in Shopware.
shopware.app_not_active_yet: The app has registered but is not activated yet — click Activate in Shopware.
shopware.app_auto_refresh: The status updates by itself once the app is activated.
shopware.app_realtime_note: New orders and payment status changes arrive right away; every 5 minutes the service also checks for changes.
shopware.app_revoke_warning: The service stops reading orders. Remove the app in Shopware too (Extensions → My extensions).
shopware.app_version_note: Because of its own bug, Shopware 6.6.10.25–6.6.10.29 cannot install apps that connect to a server — on those versions choose "Integration key". The app works on 6.7 and on 6.6 up to 6.6.10.24.
shopware.stripe_note: Money checks for Shopware currently cover PayPal (SwagPayPal). Orders paid through Stripe or other providers are shown as "payment method not supported" — no false discrepancies.
shopware.app_step_cache: Clear the Shopware cache (Settings → System → Caches & indexes → Clear cache) so that checkout observation starts on the checkout page.
shopware.app_script_note: The app also adds a small observation script to the order confirmation and «Thank you» pages. It only counts checkout stages (page shown, order sent, order placed), uses no cookies and reads no shopper data. It works when the browser check signs in as a test customer or a guest.

title.MONEY_CAPTURE_MISSING: Order marked as paid, no capture found at the provider
title.MONEY_CAPTURE_AMOUNT: Captured amount differs from the order total
title.MONEY_REFUND_MISSING: Refund in the store, not found at the provider
title.MONEY_REFUND_EXTRA: Refund at the provider that the store does not show
title.MONEY_MULTIPLE_CAPTURES: Several different captures for one order
title.MONEY_CURRENCY_MISMATCH: Capture currency differs from the order currency
title.MONEY_PAYMENT_WITHOUT_ORDER: Provider payment not matched to an order
title.CHECKOUT_FLOW_FAILED: The check did not reach the payment form
title.CHECKOUT_TEST_PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE: The test product for checks is unavailable
title.CHECKOUT_ADAPTER_UNSUPPORTED: This site's checkout is not supported by the check yet
title.INTEGRATION_STALE: The store plugin is not reporting
title.INTEGRATION_DELIVERY_DELAYED: The store plugin is sending data late
title.CHECKOUT_TEST_ACCOUNT_REJECTED: The shop does not accept the test customer sign-in
title.CHECKOUT_SUBMIT_FAILING: Customers submit the order, but no order is created

advice.MONEY_UNSUPPORTED: The order's payment method is not supported by reconciliation. Check the payment manually in the provider dashboard.
advice.MONEY_CAPTURE_MISSING: Find the transaction in the provider dashboard and check the order status. If the payment went through under another reference, match it manually. Not finding a capture does not prove the money is missing.
advice.MONEY_CAPTURE_AMOUNT: Compare the order total with the provider capture: a partial capture, an order change or a gateway error are possible.
advice.MONEY_REFUND_MISSING: Check whether the refund was actually sent through the provider and not only marked in the store.
advice.MONEY_REFUND_EXTRA: Check who issued the refund in the provider dashboard and whether the order should reflect it.
advice.MONEY_MULTIPLE_CAPTURES: Check whether the customer was charged twice. Refund if necessary.
advice.MONEY_CURRENCY_MISMATCH: Check the currency settings of the store and the payment gateway.
advice.MONEY_ORDER_CHANGED: The order was edited after payment. Make sure the final total and the capture agree.
advice.MONEY_PAYMENT_WITHOUT_ORDER: Find the payment in the provider dashboard and work out which order it belongs to. A match by amount and time is only a hint.
advice.CHECKOUT_PAYMENTS_FAILING: Try paying with this method yourself and check the payment plugin log and the provider dashboard.
advice.CHECKOUT_FLOW_FAILED: Open the site and walk the path to payment: product, cart, checkout. Look at the check screenshot. This check does not verify that charging succeeds.
advice.CHECKOUT_TEST_PRODUCT_UNAVAILABLE: Make sure the test product is published, in stock and can be added to the cart.
advice.CHECKOUT_MONITORING_BLOCKED: Site protection (WAF, CAPTCHA) blocks the check. This is not a store failure, but the store cannot be checked right now.
advice.CHECKOUT_ADAPTER_UNSUPPORTED: The theme or checkout plugins are not supported yet. This is not a store failure; we cannot check this path.
advice.INTEGRATION_STALE: Check that the site is up and the Business Watchdog plugin is active. This does not mean sales stopped, but while the plugin is silent the service cannot see orders.
advice.INTEGRATION_DELIVERY_DELAYED: The plugin is behind with sending data. Check that scheduled tasks run on the site (WP-Cron or Action Scheduler).
advice.unknown: Open the details below and check the affected part of the store.
advice.CHECKOUT_TEST_ACCOUNT_REJECTED: Check that the test customer account exists in the shop and is active, and update the e-mail and password in the check settings. This is not a shop failure; until signing in works, payment methods are not checked.
advice.CHECKOUT_SCRIPT_SILENT: The checkout page is shown, but the observation script is silent. Check the browser console on the checkout page, that the Business Watchdog plugin or app is active and that optimisation plugins or the CSP do not block it. This does not prove that customers cannot pay.
advice.CHECKOUT_SUBMIT_FAILING: Place a test order to the end and look at errors on the page and in the logs of the shop and its payment plugins: «Submit order» is sent, but no new orders and no «Thank you» page follow.

provider.title: Payment provider
provider.subtitle: Payment provider data is needed to check that order money was really captured and refunded. Without it reconciliation shows “unknown”, not “all fine”. Connect the provider your store takes payments with.
provider.why: Connect Stripe with a read-only key. The key is entered here, not in WordPress, so money data reaches us without passing through the store.
provider.step_dashboard: In Stripe open Developers → API keys → “Create restricted key”.
provider.step_permissions: Grant Read on Payment Intents, Charges and Refunds (optionally Account). No write access is needed.
provider.step_paste: Copy the key (rk_live_… or rk_test_…) and paste it below.
provider.key_hint: The key is checked for read access and stored encrypted; afterwards we only show its last 4 characters.
provider.secret_key_warning: This is a full secret key — do not enter it. Create a restricted read-only key.
provider.storage_note: Right after connecting, the store's orders of the last 90 days are reconciled again.
provider.connected: Stripe connected. The first sync runs within 15 minutes, or start it now.
provider.account_unverified: the key cannot read the account
provider.sync_incomplete: the window is finished on the next runs
provider.webhook_off: not configured — data arrives every 15 minutes
provider.polling_note: Sync runs every 15 minutes and re-reads 90 days daily; the webhook only speeds delivery up.
provider.webhook_step_add: In Stripe open Developers → Webhooks → “Add endpoint” and enter the address below.
provider.webhook_step_events: Choose the events payment_intent.*, charge.* and refund.*.
provider.webhook_step_secret: Copy the Signing secret (whsec_…) and paste it here.
provider.revoke_warning: The key will no longer be used and money reconciliation returns to “unknown”. Also delete the key in Stripe.
provider.key_rejected: Stripe rejected the key — calls to Stripe stopped and money reconciliation shows “unknown”. Disconnect this connection and connect Stripe again with a new key.

errors.stripe_secret_key_refused: This is a full secret key (sk_…). Only a restricted read-only key (rk_…) is accepted — create one in Stripe.
errors.stripe_key_invalid: This does not look like a Stripe restricted key (rk_test_… or rk_live_…).
errors.stripe_webhook_secret_invalid: The webhook secret must start with whsec_.
errors.stripe_permission_missing: The key cannot read Payment Intents, Charges or Refunds. Add the permissions and try again.
errors.stripe_key_rejected: Stripe rejected the key: it was deleted, revoked or mistyped.
errors.stripe_account_mismatch: The key belongs to a different Stripe account than the one given.
errors.provider_already_connected: Stripe is already connected to this store.
errors.stripe_unreachable: Could not reach Stripe. Try again later.
errors.stripe_rate_limited: Stripe is limiting requests for now. Try again in a minute.
errors.stripe_unavailable: Stripe is temporarily unavailable. Try again later.
errors.integration_not_active: Only an active connection can be synchronised.

paypal.why: PayPal is connected with the credentials of a separate REST app in your PayPal account. They are entered here, not in WordPress, so money data reaches the service around the store.
paypal.step_app: Open developer.paypal.com → Apps & Credentials, choose Live (or Sandbox for testing) and create an app “Business Watchdog” (type Merchant).
paypal.step_features: In the app settings untick everything and enable only Transaction Search — it is needed to list payments.
paypal.step_copy: Copy the app’s Client ID and Secret and paste them below.
paypal.warning_body: Even an app with only Transaction Search may, by PayPal’s rules, refund payments and capture authorizations. Business Watchdog never does this: the service only calls read methods from a fixed list and blocks any other request before it is sent. The credentials are stored encrypted, and you can delete the app in PayPal at any time.
paypal.acknowledge: I understand: the PayPal app credentials allow more than the service needs; the service uses them for reading only.
paypal.storage_note: Right after connecting, the store’s orders of the last 90 days are reconciled again. PayPal’s payment list lags about 1–3 hours behind.
paypal.connected: PayPal is connected. The first sync runs within 15 minutes, or start it now.
paypal.rights_note: Not used by the service: reading only, from a fixed list.
paypal.search_refreshed: PayPal payment list refreshed up to {time}
paypal.webhook_off: not set up — payments arrive from the PayPal list, up to a few hours late
paypal.polling_note: Sync runs every 15 minutes over PayPal’s transaction list and re-reads 90 days once a day; a webhook reports payments and refunds right away.
paypal.webhook_step_add: In the PayPal app open Webhooks → “Add Webhook” and enter the address below.
paypal.webhook_step_events: Select the events Payment capture completed, pending, denied, refunded, reversed and Checkout order completed.
paypal.webhook_step_id: Copy the Webhook ID of the new webhook and paste it here.
paypal.revoke_warning: The PayPal credentials stop being used; money reconciliation of PayPal orders returns to “unknown”. Delete the app in PayPal as well.
paypal.credentials_rejected: PayPal rejected the app credentials or the app lacks Transaction Search — calls to PayPal are stopped and money reconciliation shows “unknown”. Disconnect and connect PayPal again.
paypal.matching_note: Metadata matching is not supported for PayPal: payments are linked to orders only by the transaction id the PayPal plugin writes to the order.
